proposed_related_work: Recent MI-EEG domain-generalization studies seek representations that transfer to unseen subjects without target-domain training. Zhong et al. developed EEG-DG to align marginal and conditional distributions across multiple source domains [NEW_ZHONG]. Zheng et al. combined spectral-feature knowledge distillation with alignment among source-subject groups, explicitly excluding target data from training and validation in their stated setting [NEW_ZHENG]. The present study does not introduce a new domain-generalization algorithm or benchmark superiority against these methods. Its contribution is a source-only model-selection audit, participant-level heterogeneity analysis, frozen external evaluation with adverse and null results retained, complete-pipeline comparisons, and a reproducible evidence chain.
citation_warning: Do not describe EEG-DG source-only duration/checkpoint selection as independently verified. Do not transfer the performance, SOTA, mechanistic, clinical or online claims made in the cited articles to the present manuscript.
